title: Fallback routing and edge placement POC
content:
Purpose
This working proposal lays out a concrete POC for testing an edge-aware fallthrough routing pattern for a latency-sensitive customer (RetailEdge) comparing three hosting modes: hosted, dedicated, and private. Goal: prove we can meet 95th percentile inference latency <75ms for interactive storefront features while preserving cost controls and offering graceful degradation under capacity pressure.

Background/context
RetailEdge wants low-latency recommendations and chat help embedded in mobile apps. Traffic is spiky (holiday peaks) and includes PII (user IDs, order context). They prefer hosted for rapid iteration but need options for region isolation and eventual private deployment for compliance. Solutions engineering asked: can we present one routing policy that: (a) picks the best placement (edge-hosted/dedicated/private) by latency & cost; (b) automatically falls back to compatible variants when capacity or network issues occur; (c) keeps user-visible latency within bounds.

Proposed pattern (overview)
- Edge placement: a small stateless edge ingress fleet (CloudFront/Global LB) performs latency measurement and policy evaluation.
- Local routing decision: edge checks (1) geo latency to nearest hosted region, (2) recent capacity signals from dedicated pools, (3) private endpoint health (if configured). It selects a primary target and a ranked fallback list.
- Fallthrough behavior: on request failure or token-bucket saturation, route to next compatible model variant (quantized or lower-context model) or alternate deployment.
- KV/prefix caching: edge maintains short TTL prefix cache for high-frequency keys to avoid re-eval on hot paths.

Tradeoffs we will measure
- Latency vs Cost: compare per-token cost and 95/99 pctl latencies across routes. Hypothesis: dedicated gives best P95 but higher fixed cost; hosted gives best developer velocity but slightly higher P95 under burst; private gives compliance and predictable network fabric but requires customer infra.
- Consistency of responses: fallback to quantized/trimmed models can change output quality; track semantic shift with a small eval set.
- Operational complexity: more routing logic increases SRE burden, but centralizes routing rules so product teams don't manually manage deployments.

POC scope and success criteria
- Deploy prototype routing agent at the edge and integrate with: Redwood hosted API (region us-west1/us-east1), a dedicated pool (ephemeral test pool), and a private VPC endpoint (mocked in GCP test VPC).
- Traffic replay: 1M requests (mixed chat + embed) over 48 hours including synthetic holiday peak (10x baseline).
- Metrics: P95 latency <75ms for 90% of test windows, average per-request cost delta within 20% of baseline, semantic consistency score >=0.85 on eval prompts after fallback events.

Test plan details
1) Baseline measurements (hosted-only, dedicated-only, private-only).
2) Enable edge routing with simple latency-first policy. Run 24h.
3) Introduce failures: throttle dedicated pool, simulate private network outage, inject region packet loss. Validate fallbacks and measure errors and latency.
4) Evaluate quality impact: run eval harness on 100 prompts pre- and post-fallback events; compute similarity/judgement metrics.

Runbook snippets (for POC)
- Detect failure: 5xx rate >0.5% for 1m OR 3 consecutive timeouts to target -> trigger immediate failover to next route.
- Gradual rollback: if fallback increases semantic drift >0.15, auto-retry primary every 30s for 5m then return to primary if healthy.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Authorization flow: do we allow edge to forward raw payloads to private endpoint or must edge redact PII and use tokenized context? (security owns final answer)
- Cache key granularity: per-user prefix vs per-conversation? (privacy + effectiveness tradeoff)
- SLA alignment: what happens to billing attribution when fallthrough crosses customer-dedicated to hosted?

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: semantic drift when falling back to smaller models -> mitigation: quality gating and canary fallbacks only for non-critical endpoints.
- Risk: billing complexity and disputes -> mitigation: clear telemetry tagging and per-route billing metadata.
- Risk: edge becomes single point of failure -> mitigation: multi-region edge + health checks + short-circuit client fallback to local offline UX.

Deliverables and timeline (6 week POC)
- Week 1: prototype edge routing agent + routing policy spec (owner: Liam)
- Week 2: integrate hosted + dedicated test endpoints (owner: Priya)
- Week 3: implement KV prefix cache + observability dashboards (owner: Noah)
- Week 4: run baseline traffic and calibrate policies
- Week 5: inject failures and capture fallbacks, run evals
- Week 6: produce POC report and recommendations for next steps (private deployment readiness, SLA language, cost model)

Next steps (short list)
- Review with security on payload handling (Ava)
- Spin up dedicated test pool (Infra) -> JIRA SEP-1023
- Start demo script and stakeholder invite (RetailEdge PM + Eng)
